newsitem.title: UK: Dlr steady in late Europe, focus on lira ERM entry.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady in late Europe, focus on lira ERM entry.

text.p: The dollar settled into mid-ranges against the mark by late European trade with the market focus on the lira's possible ERM re-entry as soon as this weekend.

Dollar/mark was lifted above the 1.50 level in earlier trade by comments from Bundesbank council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher that the current dollar rate was not in line with the economic performance of the U.S.

"The Kuehbacher comments really gave it a lift above 1.50 but there's been no follow-through above 1.5040," said a Japanese bank dealer. "We're still in ranges but we've seen some excitement within these ranges."
By 1543 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5031/38 marks, down against its earlier session peak of 1.5040 but well above late Thursday's level of 1.4987/92 marks.

Dealers said there was little on the immediate U.S. economic data or interest rate horizon to shift the dollar out of its recent ranges so focus has shifted to the November 27 Japanese Tankan quarterly survey and developments in Europe, particularly the lira's ERM re-entry saga.
Analysts said average expectations are for a slightly weaker Tankan. This is seen as dollar positive, but markets are wary that this outcome has already been widely discounted.
The dollar was trading at 111.23/33 yen at 1606 GMT, right in the middle of the European session's narrow ranges. Late Thursday it stood at 111.38/48.

The mark slipped further against the yen, edging lower throughout European trade to test levels just above 74 in late trade. It was trading at 74.01/04 in late Europe compared with Thursday's level of 72.27/30.
Analysts said today's focus remained mainly on mark/lira after Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio confirmed today the goverment had asked to be re-admitted to the exchange rate mechanism.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi also said today the lira would be back in the ERM in a matter of "a few hours or a few days", and EU monetary officials were preparing for a monetary committee meeting on Saturday to discuss the lira's return, according to EU sources.

The mark against the lira stood at 998.10/60 lire in choppy trade, but few were willing to make any wild bets on a definite Saturday entry or at what central rate. Mark/lira stood at 999.00/999.30 late Thursday.

Attention was also on the French franc, which had recovered from two-month lows against the mark amid growing concerns about the government's franc fort policy and persistent rumours of an early-1997 cabinet reshuffle.
By late trade, the mark stood at 3.3890/94 francs, well off a session high of 3.3975 but just above late Thursday's 3.3886/90.
Sterling remained steady against the dollar and mark in late trade, still firm at $1.68 and just below 2.53 marks after an earlier bout of profit-taking.
